chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, said:

He was asked about a castrated animal: may one offer it as a sacrifice? He said: If you want meat, then it is available to you. And he said: One should not offer as a sacrifice except that by which it has been prescribed.

key_terms.أَيُضَحِّي: whether one may offer it as a ritual sacrifice
key_terms.اللَّحْمَ: meat, as distinct from the ritual validity of sacrifice
key_terms.الْخَصِيِّ: a castrated animal being asked about for sacrificial use
key_terms.عُرِّفَ بِهِ: that which has been designated or established for the sacrificial rite
key_terms.لَا يُضَحِّي: it is not valid to perform sacrifice

ai.seo_question: Can a castrated animal be offered as an udhiyah sacrifice?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the animal used for sacrifice. It distinguishes between merely seeking meat and performing the ritual sacrifice properly, indicating that sacrifice is only valid with what has been specifically recognized for that purpose.
